name: molecular-thermal-graded
description: The molecular-interfaces study's thermal-channel demonstration: the same molecular-turing-pattern Gray-Scott setup (128x128 grid, static np.random.default_rng(1) seed_uv(n=128, seed=1) u/v seed, canonical Du=0.16, Dv=0.08, F=0.037, k=0.06, dt=1.0, steps_per_tick=500) PLUS a uniform raised `temperature` field (T=1.2, embedded as a static array since composite JSON state can't call an RNG/broadcast at build time) with Ea=0.15, Tref=1.0 -- GrayScott reads `temperature` from the fields store and scales the reaction term by the elementwise Arrhenius rate factor exp(-Ea*(1/T-1/Tref)); T>Tref speeds the reaction up. Retuned from an earlier Ea=1.0/T=1.5 setting (task-3 API-map finding): that combination OVERSHOOTS -- the raised reaction rate collapses the pattern to near-uniform (v_var~=0) by 8000 total steps, which reads as 'no pattern' rather than a graded one. Ea=0.15/T=1.2 instead legibly COARSENS the pattern relative to the no-temperature flagship at the same 8000-step count: v_var drops from ~0.0119 (flagship) to ~0.0096 (thermal) -- lower but comfortably nonzero (~4.8x PATTERN_FLOOR=0.002) -- while n_domains drops from ~12 (flagship, seed-sensitive 8-12) to 2, i.e. fewer, larger domains -- a real second-modality grading of the channel, not a chemistry collapse. Verified directly with gs_step at the same seed/params in tests/test_molecular_regime.py's test_thermal_channel_grades_the_pattern.

provenance.source: task-3 molecular-interfaces thermal-channel variant (same seed_uv(n=128, seed=1) as molecular-turing-pattern, uniform T=1.5, Ea=1.0, Tref=1.0 per tests/test_gray_scott.py's test_thermal_channel_modulates_reaction_rate)
